title: Norse
capsule: This entry represents the Germanic-speaking Norse population of Scandinavia during the Roman Iron Age and Migration Period (c. 161–500 CE), before the Viking Age consolidations. Norse-speaking communities inhabited coastal Norway, Denmark, and southern Sweden, maintaining contact with the Roman Empire through trade along the amber routes, as attested by Roman imports found in Scandinavian bog deposits and the Thorsberg finds. The period saw the emergence of runic writing (Elder Futhark), the construction of monumental longhouses, and intensifying tribal confederations whose migrations contributed to the pressure on Roman frontier provinces. No unified Norse polity existed; the attestation covers a broadly defined cultural-linguistic zone.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. There was no unified Norse polity in this period; the territorial footprint is a linguistic/cultural approximation and carries very low precision as a political boundary.
